The perimeter is the arc length of the boundary curve, $L=\int_0^{2\pi}|f'(\theta)|\,d\theta$.

Differentiating gives $f'(\theta)=ie^{i\theta}+2ie^{2i\theta}+ie^{3i\theta}=ie^{i\theta}(1+e^{i\theta})^2$.

Since $|ie^{i\theta}|=1$, we get $|f'(\theta)|=|1+e^{i\theta}|^2=2+2\cos\theta$.

Therefore $L=\int_0^{2\pi}(2+2\cos\theta)\,d\theta=4\pi\approx 12.566$.

The curve is the image of the unit circle under $g(z)=z+z^2+z^3/3$. Here $g'(z)=(1+z)^2$ vanishes only at $z=-1$, which gives a cusp at $\theta=\pi$. The curve winds once around interior points, so it is a simple closed curve and the arc length equals the perimeter.

Solutions 2 and 3 derive $4\pi$ in their work but state final answers of 3 and 4, which are wrong. Solution 1 states $4\pi$ with the decimal 12.566370614359172, which is correct.
